body:
Smart Cache on ROCKNIX correctly discovers recently-played GameCube/Wii games (via .gci save mtimes / Wii NAND title dirs), but can't actually cache them: our shared native hasher (`raproxy_rchash.so`, rc_hash + libchdr) only reads raw `.iso`/`.gcm`, and ROCKNIX's entire GC/Wii library is Dolphin's own compressed `.rvz`/`.wia` format.

Android already solved this with pure Kotlin container decompression that feeds decompressed bytes into the existing native hasher (`app/src/main/java/com/raofflineproxy/proxy/hash/RvzRomDataSource.kt`, ~900 lines: WIA/RVZ header parsing, zstd group decompression, Wii AES partition decryption, hash-tree reconstruction).

Plan: port that logic to Python and wire it through the already-compiled `raproxy_hash_disc_datasource` C hook (`third_party/rcheevos_glue/rchash_glue.h`) via `ctypes.CFUNCTYPE` — no native rebuild needed.

Device check (ROCKNIX `next`, SM8550 aarch64): no pip, and neither `zstandard` nor `cryptography` Python packages are available. However both `libzstd.so.1` and `libcrypto.so.3` (OpenSSL 3) exist as system shared libraries at `/usr/lib/`, so we can bind directly via ctypes instead of vendoring wheels (consistent with the no-pip constraint that drove the pygame wheel-vendoring approach for the SDL menu).

Scope: RVZ/WIA only for now, since that's the format ROCKNIX's Dolphin actually produces/uses. GCZ/WBFS/CISO (also covered on Android) are lower priority.

Comparable effort to the Android Kotlin port — not a quick fix.
title: ROCKNIX: Smart Cache can't hash RVZ/WIA GameCube/Wii ROMs
